A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the case report is about a twin pregnancy in which the mother had pre-existing immunity to cytomegaloviruses and she got infected with the virus again.
the infection of the fetus is not related to the primary infection of the mother, and the infection of one twin may be a result of the immune response of the other twin.

The main takeaway from our work is that
recurrent maternal infection can result in symptomatic congenital cytomenegalovirus infection in the fetus, despite maternal immunity.
the risk of congenital CMV transmission is not zero in a mother with pre-existing immunity and that this risk is higher in a recurrent infection.
